Global JavaScript runs before the slot body on every key press.

The slot body and Global JavaScript share the same execution, but every tap creates a fresh QuickJS runtime and context. Do not rely on state from an earlier run.

If Global JavaScript needs input, define a helper there and pass input into it from the slot body.

This environment is synchronous-only. DOM, Node.js APIs, fetch, and async request pipelines are not available.
Only non-null return values commit text, and commit is skipped if InputConnection changed during execution.

Return contract:
- return a non-null and non-undefined value to commit it as text
- return null, return undefined, or omit return to finish without commit

Even after a successful run, text only commits when the InputConnection at the end is still the same object captured at the start. Focus changes or editor switches fail closed.
Beyond standard QuickJS features, this patch also provides input, httpRequest(options), httpGet(url), and httpPost(url, body).

Beyond standard QuickJS features, this patch provides these extra host APIs:
- input
- httpRequest(options)
- httpGet(url)
- httpPost(url, body)

httpRequest only accepts GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE. Only http:// and https:// URLs are allowed. headers must be a plain object, and body is sent as UTF-8.

Non-2xx status, invalid method, invalid URL scheme, timeout, invalid headers, transport errors, and response bodies over the configured limit all throw script errors.
Slots are clamped by global timeout, response, memory, and stack limits; syntax and runtime errors fail only that run.

Runtime limits:
- slot timeoutMs input must stay within 0..global timeoutMaxMs; after sanitize the runtime minimum is 1 ms
- response body limit, memory limit, and max stack come from JavaScript Runtime Limits

Defaults:
- timeoutMaxMs: 30000 ms
- response body: 1 MiB
- memory: 8 MiB
- max stack: 512 KiB

Syntax errors, runtime errors, timeouts, HTTP failures, oversized responses, and InputConnection changes fail closed for the current run only. They do not disable the whole Custom Top Row feature.

Dictionary and model resources for Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Korean and related input methods. Switching may affect word conversion, candidate ranking and continuation predictions for input such as Zhuyin and Pinyin.

Dictionaries and language models for English, German, Thai and many other languages. Switching may affect suggested vocabulary, spelling correction, candidate ranking and next-word suggestions. Next-word prediction: an additional American English engine that suggests following words from the text already entered. It does not replace the main dictionary; disabling it does not disable every source of next-word suggestions.
A Google American English TFLite model used for input-correction triggering, separate from the main dictionary. Presets apply the matching TFLite enable and key-routing flags together.

Auxiliary models and biasing dictionaries retrieved by the Gboard user-feature-cache manager. This catalog provides American English, German, Spanish and French resources, rather than the main Traditional Chinese model. This selects resource configuration; Gboard controls usage conditions. Native SAFT version detection is not yet available.
Separate data for Japanese spelling-correction suggestions. It is independent of the main kana-to-kanji dictionary. Selecting resources does not enable system spell checking.

Grammar correction resources for supported languages such as English, Spanish, French and Portuguese. These affect sentence error detection and correction suggestions. Selecting resources here does not enable the Grammar Checker feature.

Identifies the likely language of multilingual input to help select suggestions from the appropriate language. It is not a dictionary and does not add input languages; switching may affect language decisions for multilingual suggestions.
